meta.title: Many languages, many homes
meta.summary: English is only part of what you’ll hear here. Ohio’s families and communities bring many languages into classrooms, neighborhoods, and everyday conversations. What a lovely chorus.

sourceRefs.label: Ohio Department of Education and Workforce · English Learners
University of Akron · Holmes County language study

blocks.text: Ohio’s education department lists Spanish, Somali, Arabic, Swahili, Chinese, Japanese, Nepali, Pennsylvania Dutch, French, Turkish, and many other home languages among the state’s English learners. That list describes a school population, not a ranking of every language spoken statewide; still, it opens a wonderful window onto the variety and people behind it.

Pennsylvania Dutch also has a particular history in some Amish and Mennonite communities, with local differences in how languages are used. A University of Akron repository study looks specifically at a Holmes County Beachy Amish-Mennonite community. Let’s keep that specificity: language can connect people, while each family and community has its own experience.
